revision_summary: No fabricated quotes were found (all passed the deterministic check), so this is not a rerun-from-scratch situation, but several classification and schema-reference issues need targeted fixes: (1) The spouse_handling classification at 05:04 misapplies protocols.spouse_decision \u2014 that protocol is about decision-deferral ('I need to talk to my spouse'), not bill-payment knowledge ('my wife takes care of the bills'). Reclassify as a co-decision-maker identification gap without invoking the formal spouse_decision trigger, or cite a more accurate schema anchor. (2) The prior_contact_probe_miss moments at 01:12 and 04:05 cite rebuttals.already_saw_design, which is a mismatched schema reference (that rebuttal addresses comparison-shopping, not competitor-ghosting frustration) \u2014 note this as an uncovered schema gap instead of citing an ill-fitting existing rebuttal id. (3) Tone down 'trust gift' language for the competitor-ghosting complaint in multi_touch_patterns \u2014 reserve that phrase for actual vulnerability disclosures per the schema's defined categories (health/financial/family loss), not routine service complaints. (4) Add the 00:40 quote ('Mount Airy? We have teams out there, but I'm in Utah...') to the intro_legitimacy_omission moment as the clearer example of the rep's improvised (non-protocol) response to the spam suspicion. (5) Surface the 07:12\u201308:12 dead-air/cutoff moment explicitly as a distinct tech-friction or call-drop event, since it's ambiguous whether the customer hung up or the call technically dropped \u2014 this affects both outcome framing and coaching (dropped call vs. customer disengagement are different problems). (6) Reconsider the setter_scope_creep classification at 06:28 \u2014 the rep's actual words are a brief, non-technical bill-swap summary in direct response to a customer cost question, which is closer to acceptable minimal anchoring than a clear scope violation; the alternative_hypothesis already offered undercuts the primary classification and should be weighted more heavily.
